samples.L1: This week, a buyer borrowing $320,000 can take a 15-year mortgage at 6.73%, or a 30-year at 7.40% and pay it off in 15 years anyway, keeping the lower required payment as a fallback. We replay every week of US mortgage rates since 1991 to put a dollar price on that fallback, and to show what each extra dollar of principal actually earns: the bar any other use of that money has to clear. History, not a forecast: it won't tell you which loan to take, or whether to invest.
samples.L2: Pay extra on the mortgage, or invest the difference? Each extra dollar of principal earns exactly the loan's rate, so the answer starts with that rate. We follow a buyer borrowing $320,000 this week who can take a 15-year loan at 6.73%, or a 30-year at 7.40% paid off in 15 years, and replay every week of US mortgage rates since 1991: what the 30-year's lower fallback payment has cost, and how high the prepayment bar has been. History, not a forecast: no loan or investment pick.

roles.T: You are an American about to buy a home with a mortgage of about $320,000. You can afford a 15-year payment, and you wonder whether to take a 30-year loan and pay extra, or invest the spare cash.
